method: TypeSafe System One (model jev-latest), one question per call, three repetitions per question, medians reported; the question set was put to the verifier in the general form of the policy invariants, without any information about the sessions on which the benchmark was run

questions.statement: the goal statement of a session must be preserved verbatim by any compaction
user correction rounds of a debug loop are high-value and must never be dropped
assistant records stating why a previous attempt failed are high-value evidence for the next rounds of the loop
dropping the only surviving copy of a command's final result causes the continuation to hallucinate or re-ask
an LLM summary alone, without verbatim preservation, is sufficient to continue a long correction loop without a handover
a keep/drop classifier should be allowed to rewrite user conversation text to save space
which single measure most raises the chance that a compacted session continues without a handover
storage risk of force-keeping the last result of every distinct command line on re-run heavy sessions
with the policy layered over the classifier, a compacted session can continue without any manual handover document
the last-result pin should apply only where the result carries critical evidence (tallies, hashes, errors, build verdicts)
preferred pinning regime for sessions dominated by a long correction loop over a small part of a big goal
questions.note: contrary to r8 and r10; outvoted by them, the two being the stronger grounds - shipped default pinLast=critical, with always available behind the --pin-last flag
